title: Satapatha Brahmana
altTitles: The Brahmana of One Hundred Paths
attributionNote: The Satapatha Brahmana is an anonymous Vedic prose text attached to the White Yajurveda. Its teaching is traditionally ascribed to Yajnavalkya, but the work is a collective priestly composition.
description: The Satapatha Brahmana is the longest and most important of the Vedic Brahmanas, in fourteen kandas. It explains the ritual of the White Yajurveda — the fire altar, the soma sacrifice, the horse sacrifice, the agnihotra and the royal consecration — and embeds in its exegesis the creation hymns, the doctrine of the sacrifice as the making of the world, and the earliest form of the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad. It is the bridge between the Vedic hymns and the Upanishads.
historicalContext: The Satapatha survives in the Madhyandina and Kanva recensions; Eggeling translated the Madhyandina text for the Sacred Books of the East in five volumes (12, 26, 41, 43 and 44; 1882–1900). His is still the only complete English translation.
availabilityNote: Complete. All fourteen kandas of Eggeling's translation are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time. Each printed brahmana is one chapter, labelled with its kanda, adhyaya and brahmana numbers, so the five printed volumes are read as one work. The volumes' introductions are not part of the work.
